Prevention: Keep onion fields and borders free of weeds.
Remove and destroy volunteer onion plants and debris that may harbour thrips.
Avoid planting onions near cereal fields because they are alternate hosts for thrips.
Irrigate the field regulary as overhead irrigation and rainfall suppress thrips popualations.
Plant carrots into the onion field, because thrips do not like them.
Avoid planting onions near an existing infested field.
Mulch onion fields as this helps reduce the thrips population.
Monitoring: Visit field regularly to look for flea-sized yellow-brown insects (1.3mm) once every three days after second week of planting, particularly during dry season.
Check leaves for symptom development e.g. silver, white blotches and streaks in the leaves, leaves turn yellow and are brown at the tips.
With severe injury, plants wither and bulbs are small and misshapen.
Carry out control methods when a threshold of an average of 3-5 thrips per plant is reached.
Yellow or blue sticky traps can be used to monitor the number of adult thrips.
Direct Control: Remove heavily infested plant material and burn.
